title: Cross-Regime Measurement Failure in the KT3b Environmental Test
abstract: Analyzes the null result of the KT3b environmental mass-scaling test in Energy-Flow Cosmology and shows that the monotonic signal collapse across increasingly rigorous runs is explained by a cross-regime measurement inconsistency. It identifies explicit violations of the Regime-Consistent Measurement Principle (driver–response mismatch, boundary observation, and mass-model mixing), and proposes three RCMP-consistent test architectures as a methodological diagnosis stronger than the null result itself.
